questions.question: What does a list in ServiceNow display?

options.text: A single record from a table
Records from a table where each row is a record and each column is a field
Only the fields marked as mandatory
Configuration settings for applications

explanation.correct: A list shows records from a table. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field. Lists can be interacted with in various ways including filtering and sorting. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: A single record is displayed on a form, not a list. Lists show multiple records.
Lists show all configured fields, not just mandatory ones.
Configuration settings are managed in different modules, not in lists.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A list shows records from a table. On the ServiceNow platform, lists can be interacted with in various ways. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field.

questions.question: What is the purpose of views in ServiceNow?

options.text: To delete records from the database
To display lists or forms in different ways for different user types
To create new tables automatically
To import data from external sources

explanation.correct: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users. The number of records stays the same, but field order may vary. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Views don't delete records; they only control how data is displayed.
Table creation is a separate administrative function.
Data import is handled by Import Sets, not views.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users.

questions.question: An incident list shows the breadcrumb All > Active = true > Category = Software > Priority = 2. A user clicks the Category = Software breadcrumb. What happens?

options.text: The Priority = 2 condition is removed and the list shows active Software incidents
Only the Category = Software condition is removed
All conditions are removed
The list is grouped by Category

explanation.correct: Breadcrumbs are ordered from most general (left) to most specific (right). Clicking a breadcrumb removes all the conditions to its right. Clicking the condition separator (>) before a condition removes only that condition. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_UsingFiltersAndBreadcrumbs.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Removing only one condition is done by clicking the separator (>) before that condition, not the breadcrumb itself.
Clicking All removes all conditions; clicking another breadcrumb keeps it and the conditions to its left.
Breadcrumbs filter; they do not group the list.

source.excerpt: Clicking a breadcrumb removes all the conditions to its right.

questions.question: A user right-clicks the value 'In Progress' in the State column of a list and selects Filter Out. Which statement about the result is correct?

options.text: It adds State != In Progress as the most specific condition, and records with an empty State still display
It removes all conditions and shows only In Progress records
It deletes the In Progress records from the list
It adds State = In Progress to the filter

explanation.correct: Quick filters add a condition to the right of the current breadcrumb. Filter Out builds [field] [is not] [value] or [field] [is] [empty], so records with empty or null values still display. A manually built 'is not' filter does not add the empty condition automatically. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_QuickFilters.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Quick filters add a condition; they don't clear the existing filter.
Filtering never deletes records.
Show Matching adds State = In Progress; Filter Out adds the opposite.

source.excerpt: Records that contain empty or null values still display in the filtered list.

questions.question: An administrator is filtering a list of active incidents and clicks New. What happens to the new record?

options.text: It is preset with values from the list filter, such as Active selected
It opens blank; filters never affect new records
It copies every field from the first record in the list
The filter is cleared before the form opens

explanation.correct: Clicking New in a filtered list automatically applies the same filter to the new record. For example, in a list filtered for active, priority 1 incidents, New opens a record preset with Active selected and Priority set to 1 - Critical. The dictionary attribute ignore_filter_on_new=true stops this for a field. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_UsingFiltersAndBreadcrumbs.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The filter conditions are applied as preset values on the new record.
Only the filter conditions are applied, not values from another record.
The filter is used to preset values, not cleared.

source.excerpt: Clicking the New button in a filtered list automatically applies the same filter to the new record.

questions.question: A manager wants one list that shows active Hardware incidents AND inactive Software incidents. Which condition builder feature produces results in the form (A and B) or (C and D)?

options.text: A top-level OR condition
A dependent OR condition
A quick filter
Grouping the list by Category

explanation.correct: Top-level OR conditions work as (A and B) or (C and D), so you can show the results of several condition sets in one list. Dependent OR conditions work as A and (B or C), giving alternatives for a single condition. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_UsingORConditions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A dependent OR works in the manner A and (B or C).
Quick filters add simple AND conditions to the breadcrumb.
Grouping aggregates records by a field; it does not combine condition sets.

source.excerpt: Top level OR conditions work in the manner (A and B) or (C and D).

questions.question: A user wants to create a tag that every user in the instance can see. What does this require?

options.text: Setting Viewable by to Everyone, which is available to users with the admin or tags_admin role
Setting Viewable by to Me
Adding the tag to an update set
Creating the tag from the Tagged Documents page only

explanation.correct: The Viewable by setting controls a tag's sharing level: Me (private), Groups and Users (shared), or Everyone (global). The Everyone option is available to users with the admin or tags_admin role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_Tags.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Me makes a private tag that only the owner can see.
Update sets do not control tag visibility.
The sharing level, not where the tag is created, controls visibility.

source.excerpt: Global tag, visible to everyone. This option is available to users with the admin or tags_admin role.

questions.question: Where are tags stored, and where can a user see the tags they have created?

options.text: In the Tag [label] table; users can see their tags under Self-Service > My Tags
In the sys_tags table; only admins can view them
In the user's preferences; they can't be listed
In the Knowledge Base; under Knowledge > Tags

explanation.correct: Tags are text labels that group and organize items such as records. They are stored in the Tag [label] table and can be listed under System Definition > Tags or Self-Service > My Tags. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_Tags.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The documented table is Tag [label], and users can view their own tags.
Tags are records in the Tag [label] table, not user preferences.
Tags are not stored in the Knowledge Base.

source.excerpt: Tags are stored in the Tag [label] table. To view tags in a list, navigate to System Definition > Tags or Self-Service > My Tags.

questions.question: What does grouping a list by a field do?

options.text: It aggregates the list by that field and displays the record count per group
It permanently sorts the underlying table
It creates a new database view
It hides all records that have an empty value in that field

explanation.correct: Grouping aggregates a list by a field and displays the record count per group. You can group from the list title context menu or by right-clicking a column heading and selecting Group By. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_GroupedLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Grouping changes only the list display, not the table.
Database views are created separately by administrators.
Grouping does not filter records out.

source.excerpt: Grouping aggregates a list by a field and displays the record count per group.

questions.question: An agent needs to change three different fields, including one not shown in the list, on 20 records at once. Which method does the documentation recommend?

options.text: Edit multiple records using an editing form
Use the list editor on each cell
Use a quick filter
Personalize the list

explanation.correct: The list editor is quickest for setting one field to the same value on multiple records. To edit multiple fields, or fields that don't appear in the list view, use an editing form. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/r_MethodsForListEdits.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The list editor is best for updating a single field that appears in the list.
Quick filters narrow the list; they don't edit records.
Personalizing a list changes columns for the user; it doesn't edit data.

source.excerpt: If you want to edit multiple fields or fields that don’t appear in the list view, use an editing form.

questions.question: A user with the personalize_list role selects Wrap column text and Compact rows while personalizing the Incident list. Where do these display options apply?

options.text: To all lists for that user, not just the view being personalized
Only to the Incident list for that user
To the Incident list for every user
To all lists for every user

explanation.correct: Personal list customizations don't affect what other users see. The display options such as Wrap column text and Compact rows apply to all lists, not just the view you are personalizing. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The column selection applies to the specific list view, but these display options apply to all lists.
Personal list changes never affect other users.
Personal list changes never affect other users.

source.excerpt: These options apply to all lists, not just the view you’re personalizing.

questions.question: On a new incident form, what is the difference between Insert and Insert and Stay in the form context menu?

options.text: Insert saves the new record and returns to the previous page; Insert and Stay saves and displays the new record
Insert saves a draft; Insert and Stay publishes the record
Insert creates a template; Insert and Stay creates a record
There is no difference

explanation.correct: In the form context menu, Insert saves the data as a new record and returns to the previously viewed page. Insert and Stay saves and displays the new record. Save saves changes without leaving the form view. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_FormContextMenu.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Neither option creates drafts; both insert a record.
Templates are created from the template bar, not with Insert.
The two options behave differently after saving.

source.excerpt: Saves the data as a new record and returns to the previously viewed page. … Saves and displays the new record.

questions.question: An administrator has filled in an incident form exactly as it should look when others use it as a starting point. How can they save it as a template?

options.text: Use the plus icon (+) in the template bar, name the template, and save
Select Insert and Stay
Right-click the header and select Show XML
Export the form to PDF

explanation.correct: To create a template by saving a form, toggle the template bar so it is visible, complete the form, select the plus icon (+) in the template bar, enter a descriptive name, and save. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_SaveAFormAsATemplateInUI16OrUI15.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Insert and Stay saves a record, not a template.
Show XML displays record data in XML format.
Export to PDF creates a document, not a template.

documentation.section: Create a template by saving a form

source.excerpt: In the template bar, click the plus icon (+).

questions.question: Which form context menu options are available only to administrators? (Choose two.)

options.text: Show XML
Copy sys_id
Save
Reload Form
Insert

explanation.correct: Show XML, Copy sys_id, and History are administrator-only options in the form context menu. Save, Insert, and Reload Form are general options. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_FormContextMenu.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Save is a general option that saves changes without leaving the form.
Reload Form reloads the record from the database and is not admin-only.
Insert saves a new record and is not admin-only.

source.excerpt: Administrators only. Displays record data in XML format. … Administrators only. Copies to the clipboard the sys_id of the record.

questions.question: What happens when a user switches the view on a form they are editing?

options.text: The form is submitted, saving all changes and running any onSubmit client scripts
The changes are discarded
The record becomes read-only until reloaded
The form opens in a new browser tab

explanation.correct: Switching views submits the form, which saves all changes and triggers any onSubmit client scripts. You cannot switch form views on a new form that has not been saved yet. The selected view is saved as a user preference. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Changes are saved, not discarded.
Switching views doesn't make the record read-only.
The view changes in place; no new tab is opened.

source.excerpt: Switching views submits the form, which saves all changes and triggers any onSubmit client scripts that apply.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, which tool does ServiceNow recommend for configuring forms because it includes all Form Designer and Form Layout options?

options.text: Form Builder
Schema Map
List Editor
Theme Builder

explanation.correct: Starting with Australia, Form Designer is being prepared for future deprecation. ServiceNow recommends configuring forms with Form Builder, which has all of the Form Designer and Form Layout options plus other features. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Schema Map shows table relationships.
The List Editor edits field values in lists.
Theme Builder manages Next Experience themes.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Australia release, form designer is being prepared for future deprecation. … Form Builder has all of the Form Designer and Form Layout options.

questions.question: An administrator enters task.list in the navigation filter and selects New. What happens?

options.text: The Task Interceptor asks which task child table to create the record in, because tasks aren't created directly on the Task table
A record is created directly in the Task table
An error appears because the Task table can't be opened
A new child table is created

explanation.correct: Tasks aren't created directly on the Task [task] table. Instead, they are created on task child tables such as Incident or Problem. Selecting New from task.list opens the Task Interceptor, where you choose the child table. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_TaskTable.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Task records are created on child tables, not directly on Task.
task.list opens normally.
New creates a record, not a table.

source.excerpt: Tasks aren't created directly on the Tasks [task] table. Instead, tasks are created on task child tables.

questions.question: An administrator adds a new field to the Task [task] table. Which tables get the field?

options.text: All tables that extend Task, such as Incident and Problem
Only the Task table
Only tables in the same application scope
Only tables that are not yet in use

explanation.correct: Modifications made to the Task table are applied to all child tables. Adding fields is low-impact because you can hide them where they aren't needed, but deleting fields used across tables can cause data loss. Dictionary overrides can change some parts of a field definition for specific child tables. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_TaskTable.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Child tables inherit fields from Task.
Inheritance follows the table hierarchy, not the application scope.
All child tables inherit the field, whether or not they have data.

source.excerpt: Modifications made to the Tasks [task} table are applied to all child tables.

questions.question: Which task journal fields are described in the Task table structure documentation? (Choose two.)

options.text: Additional comments, which any user can update
Work notes, which ITIL users can update
Short description, which only admins can update
Assignment group, which is a journal field
Priority, which is a journal field

explanation.correct: Journal fields are multi-line text boxes that add comments to the Activity field with a notation when saved. Additional comments can be updated by any user; Work notes can be updated by ITIL users. The activity formatter displays them with record changes and notifications sent. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_JournalFields.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Short description is a string field, not a journal field.
Assignment group is a reference field, not a journal field.
Priority is a choice field, not a journal field.

source.excerpt: Additional comments|Any user can update. … Work notes|ITIL users can update.

questions.question: How do data lookup rules differ from the Assignment rules module?

options.text: Data lookup rules can change any field value, not just assignment fields, and have more options for when they run
Data lookup rules can only set the Assignment group
Data lookup rules run only on the Task table itself
Data lookup rules replace business rules

explanation.correct: Data lookup rules offer a generic way to change any field value, not just assignment fields. They can run on form change, record insert, or record update, and can optionally replace existing values. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DataLookupRules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Setting only assignment fields describes the Assignment rules module.
Data lookup rules aren't limited to the Task table.
Business rules still exist; data lookup rules are a separate mechanism.

source.excerpt: Data lookup rules offer a generic way to change any field value, not just assignment fields.

questions.question: Which three types of Visual Task Boards can users create?

options.text: Freeform, flexible, and guided
Personal, group, and global
Kanban, Scrum, and Waterfall
List, form, and calendar

explanation.correct: There are three types of Visual Task Boards. Freeform boards show any task records, including personal tasks. Flexible boards show tasks that match a filter and allow custom lanes. Guided boards are like flexible boards, but their lanes correspond to field values and generally can't be edited. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/visual-task-boards/vtb-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: These describe sharing levels, not VTB types.
These are delivery methodologies, not VTB types.
These are UI views, not VTB types.

source.excerpt: There are three types of Visual Task Boards.

questions.question: A support manager wants a board whose lanes always match the incident State values, with cards removed automatically when incidents no longer match the filter. Which board type fits best?

options.text: Guided board
Freeform board
Personal task list
Report dashboard

explanation.correct: Guided boards are data driven and similar to flexible boards, except that their lanes correspond to field values, such as State, and in most cases can't be edited. Filter-based boards remove cards automatically when tasks no longer match the filter conditions. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/visual-task-boards/vtb-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Freeform boards use lanes and cards that members add and remove manually.
A personal task list isn't a Visual Task Board type.
Dashboards show analytics, not interactive task cards in lanes.

source.excerpt: Similar to flexible boards except that guided board lanes correspond to field values and cannot be edited in most cases.

questions.question: Which statement about access to Visual Task Boards is correct?

options.text: Visual task boards aren't available to external users; for other users, ACLs determine board access and card visibility
Every user, including external users, can see every board
Only admins can view boards
Board access is controlled only by update sets

explanation.correct: Visual task boards aren't available to external users. For other user roles, access control rules (ACLs) determine both board access and card visibility. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/visual-task-boards/exploring-vis-task-boards.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: External users can't use Visual Task Boards.
Non-admin users can use boards, subject to ACLs.
ACLs control access, not update sets.

source.excerpt: Visual task boards aren't available to external users. For other user roles, access control rules (ACLs) determine both board access and card visibility.

questions.question: An administrator is creating an email notification. Which Notification form tabs define its trigger, its recipients, and its content?

options.text: When to send, Who will receive, and What it will contain
Conditions, Actions, and Script
Trigger, Audience, and Template only
Schedule, Approvers, and Variables

explanation.correct: The Notification form uses the When to send tab (conditions), the Who will receive tab (recipients), and the What it will contain tab (content). A What Digest will contain tab appears when Allow Digest is selected. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are not the tab names on the Notification form.
The documented tabs are When to send, Who will receive, and What it will contain.
These are not the tab names on the Notification form.

source.excerpt: When to send — Conditions required to send the notification. … Who will receive — Recipients of the notification. … What it will contain — Contents of the notification.

questions.question: An administrator wants every task type to send the same notification and selects the Task [task] table on a new email notification. What does the documentation advise?

options.text: Don't select the Task table; notifications that run directly on Task aren't supported, so link the notification to a specific table such as Incident
Selecting Task is the recommended way to cover all child tables
Task is allowed only for event-based notifications
Task can be selected if the notification weight is 0

explanation.correct: The documentation says not to select the Task [task] table for a notification. That table exists to be extended, and notifications that run on the Task table directly aren't supported. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The documentation explicitly advises against using the Task table.
No exception is documented for event-based notifications.
The weight doesn't change table support.

source.excerpt: Don’t select the Task [task] table. This table is for extending other tables. Notifications that run on the Task table directly aren’t supported.

questions.question: An agent adds a comment to an incident and closes it shortly after. Both 'Incident commented' and 'Incident closed' would notify the caller. Assuming the notifications have different weights, what happens?

options.text: Only the notification with the highest weight is sent
Both notifications are always sent
Neither is sent because they conflict
The notification created first is sent

explanation.correct: Notifications with the same target table and recipients are treated as duplicates. With different weights, the system sends only the notification with the highest weight, which in the documented example is Incident Closed. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Duplicate notifications are consolidated by weight.
The system resolves duplicates by sending the highest-weight notification.
Weight, not creation order, decides which is sent.

source.excerpt: The system only sends the notification with the highest weight

questions.question: Which options are available in the Send when field of an email notification? (Choose three.)

options.text: Record inserted or updated
Event is fired
Triggered by a Notification step in Flow Designer
When a user logs in
When a report is viewed

explanation.correct: Send when can be set to send the notification when a record is inserted or updated, when a particular event is fired, or when triggered by a Notification step in Flow Designer. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: User login is not a Send when option.
Viewing a report is not a Send when option.

source.excerpt: When a record is inserted or updated … When a particular event is fired … When Notification step in Flow Designer

questions.question: A notification is sent to a group, but the group members don't receive individual emails. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Include members is not selected on the group record
The group has no manager
The notification weight is too high
The notification was built on the Incident table

explanation.correct: When groups are selected as recipients, group members receive individual notifications only if Include members is selected in the group record. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Individual delivery depends on the Include members setting, not on having a manager.
Weight resolves duplicates; it doesn't stop group delivery.
Incident is a valid notification table.

source.excerpt: Group members receive individual notifications only if Include members is selected in the group record.

questions.question: Which statement about notification recipients and access controls is correct?

options.text: The system doesn't exclude recipients based on access controls, so recipients can receive email about records they can't normally access
Recipients who fail ACLs are automatically removed
Notifications are only sent to users with the admin role
ACLs are checked on every email address in the Users field

explanation.correct: The system doesn't exclude recipients based on access controls. Recipients can receive email about records they can't normally access in the UI, so avoid the Subscribable option and review content for sensitive records. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Recipients are not filtered by ACLs.
Any active user with a valid email address can receive notifications.
ACLs are not evaluated for notification recipients.

source.excerpt: The system doesn’t exclude recipients based on access controls.

questions.question: By default, what does an inbound email action do when it receives an email with no identifiable watermark?

options.text: It attempts to create an incident from the message
It discards the email
It forwards the email to the system administrator
It creates a knowledge article

explanation.correct: An inbound email action checks the email for a watermark that links it to a task. By default, an email with no identifiable watermark makes an inbound email action try to create an incident. An email with the watermark of an existing incident updates that incident. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_InboundEmailActions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The default action creates an incident; it does not discard the email.
No default forwarding to administrators is described.
Inbound email actions don't create knowledge articles by default.

source.excerpt: By default, if an email has no identifiable watermark, an inbound email action attempts to create an incident from the message.

questions.question: What is dot-walking in ServiceNow?

options.text: A method to delete multiple records at once
Collecting data from related tables via reference fields
A type of user authentication
A workflow execution pattern

explanation.correct: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It works in form layout, but not in form design. It's commonly used in form builder, list views, platform analytics, and Workflow Studio. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_DotWalking.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Deleting records is done through list editing or bulk delete, not dot-walking.
Authentication is managed separately and unrelated to dot-walking.
Workflow execution follows different patterns; dot-walking is about data relationships.

documentation.section: Dot-walking to data in related tables

source.excerpt: Dot-walking provides access to fields on related tables from a form, list, or script.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

questions.question: What are the three parts of a filter condition in ServiceNow?

options.text: Table, Record, and Value
Field, Operator, and Value
User, Role, and Permission
Name, Description, and Category

explanation.correct: A filter condition has three parts: Field (can include related tables), Operator (varies by field type, like 'greater than' for numbers), and Value (text entry or choice list based on field type). See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While tables and records are concepts in ServiceNow, they're not the three parts of a filter condition.
User, Role, and Permission relate to security, not filter conditions.
These are common field types but not the components of a filter condition.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A filter condition has three parts. Field-- able to be chosen based on user access, can include related tables. Operator-- varies by field type. Value-- text entry or choice list based on field.

questions.question: What is the difference between personalize list and configure list layout?

options.text: They are the same function with different names
Personalize list affects only the individual user; configure list layout affects everyone
Personalize list is for admins only; configure list layout is for all users
Personalize list is permanent; configure list layout is temporary

explanation.correct: Where the list layout configuration affects everyone, the personalize list modifies the layout of a list for an individual user. It does not affect the platform default. Personalization should be used for temporary situations. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: They have different scopes - one affects all users, one affects only the individual.
The distinction is about scope of changes, not user permissions.
Actually, personalization persists for the user, but system changes override it.

questions.question: What does a form in ServiceNow display?

options.text: Multiple records from multiple tables
Information from a single record in a table
Only read-only data
System configuration settings

explanation.correct: Forms in ServiceNow show information from a single record in a table, and can be accessed through global search or lists. The form's content varies with the record type, and users can view or edit this content. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Forms show a single record; lists show multiple records.
Forms can contain both read-only and editable fields based on configuration.
System configuration has dedicated modules; forms display record data.

questions.question: What is the purpose of templates in ServiceNow?

options.text: To create new tables automatically
To pre-fill common field values when creating records
To backup database records
To generate automated reports

explanation.correct: Templates allow users to fill in the most common fields for a table, save it as a template, and make it available to users. Users can apply templates manually when creating records, or administrators can set scripts to apply them automatically. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Table creation is separate from templates.
Backups are handled by different system functions.
Reports are generated separately, not through templates.

questions.question: A user wants to hide certain fields on a form without affecting other users. Which feature should they use?

options.text: Form Builder
Form Layout
Personalize Form
UI Policy

explanation.correct: Personalize Form allows individual users to hide fields on a form without affecting other users. The personalized form remains each time the user logs in. Mandatory fields cannot be hidden. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_FormPersonalizationAdmin.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Form Builder modifies the form for all users, not just the individual.
Form Layout changes affect all users viewing that form.
UI Policies can hide fields but affect all users matching the conditions, not just individual personalization.

source.excerpt: Personalizing a form in this way modifies the form for you only. To make changes to a form that are visible to all users, you must configure the form.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature automatically sets the Assigned to and Assignment group fields on tasks when a set of conditions is met?

options.text: Data Policies
Assignment Rules
Business Rules
UI Policies

explanation.correct: Assignment Rules automatically assign incidents to specific users or groups based on matching conditions like category, configuration item, or location. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_AssignmentRulesModule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data Policies enforce data quality by making fields mandatory or read-only, not for assignment.
While Business Rules can perform assignments, Assignment Rules are specifically designed for this purpose and are easier to configure.
UI Policies control form behavior like showing/hiding fields, not record assignment.

source.excerpt: The Assignment rules module allows you to automatically set a value in the assigned_to and assignment_group fields when a set of conditions occurs.
